title: Introduce auth-saga credential flow and cross-SDK pullstream ergonomics
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Introduce an 'auth-saga' orchestration for credential lifecycle + small ergonomic improvements to pullstream APIs across Python/TS/Go. SDKs bumped: python v1.13.0, typescript v2.7.0, go v1.5.2. Backwards-compatible helpers provided for migration.
description:
Context and motivation: We keep seeing duplicated reauth logic and subtle drift between SDKs that leads to production flakes (token races during high-concurrency streaming). This PR introduces an "auth-saga" orchestration: a small, opinionated credential lifecycle coordinator that centralizes refresh/priming/heartbeat logic and exposes a lightweight, language-idiomatic pullstream adapter. The goal is to reduce duplicated logic across SDKs, simplify backoff/resume semantics for consumers, and make cross-SDK behavior deterministic under load.

What this PR does (single-string summary):
- Add a compact auth-saga implementation (coordination + profiles) that supports adaptive reauth profiles (fast/normal/conservative) and prefetch priming for long-running streams.
- Introduce a typed pullstream adapter in TypeScript and matching ergonomic facades in Python and Go. These expose a small set of guarantees: resume tokens, deterministic backoff profiles, and an explicit "prime" hook.
- Wire telemetry hooks: cred.lifecycle.* and stream.adapter.* metrics (counts/timings/error-codes).
- Small API refinements to StreamClient constructors to accept an optional AuthSagaConfig without breaking existing constructors.
- Bump SDK versions and update changelogs.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked in ENG-4281
- [x] Implement core auth-saga in typescript (shared impl used by console tooling)
- [x] Py/Go facades that call into established rpc surface and reuse existing token providers
- [x] Unit tests for credential race scenarios and resume semantics
- [x] Integration test: simulated token expiry during stream (flaky on initial run, see CI notes)
- [x] Docs snippet and migration notes in SDK CHANGELOGs

Commits (high-level):
- feat(auth-saga): add core saga state machine and profile registry
- feat(stream): typed pullstream adapter (ts) + py/go wrappers
- chore(sdk): bump versions, changelogs, and examples

Files/areas touched (high-level):
- sdk/typescript/src/auth/saga.ts (new)
- sdk/typescript/src/stream/pullstream-adapter.ts (new)
- sdk/python/redwood/auth_saga.py (facade)
- sdk/go/redwood/authsaga.go (facade)
- sdk/*/CHANGELOG.md (updated)
- docs/sdks/auth-saga.md (new quickstart)
- tests/integration/stream_reauth_simulation.test.ts
- ci: small pipeline addition to run auth-saga integration in sandbox

Notable implementation details and decisions:
- The "saga" name indicates orchestration only: it does not replace customer-managed token providers. Instead it composes with them and offers a standardized prefetch/heartbeat/decay strategy.
- Profiles are simple JSON presets (fast/normal/conservative) tuned for typical PLG, enterprise, and dedicated throughput patterns. They map to TTL thresholds and retry backoff windows.
- Pullstream guarantees: single in-flight reauth attempt per saga instance, explicit resume token emission on recoverable errors, and an opt-in "primeOnOpen" flag to warm caches. These make it easier to reason about ordering and idempotency at application layer.
- Backwards compatibility: existing StreamClient constructors are preserved. An optional new config object is accepted; when omitted behavior matches previous SDK versions.

Review conversation (abridged transcript embedded into the single description string):
- Ethan Li: "Approach looks good; two concerns: metric cardinality for lifecycle labels and edge case around token churn on bursty traffic."
- Author (Priya): "Addressed metrics by capping label dimension to {profile, outcome} and added an internal aggregation. For churn I added a soft-debounce in the saga (100ms) to avoid thundering reauths. See commit feat(auth-saga): debounce reauth."
- Sofia Ramirez: "Can we avoid changing public type names in TS? Consumers might import StreamAdapter directly."
- Author: "Maintained original names, introduced small compat shims (exported in index.ts) and added a short snippet in CHANGELOG showing imports before/after."
- Marco Duarte: "Integration test was flaky in the first CI run; test harness was missing a mock kube dns timer."
- Author: "Fixed harness and pinned a stable clock in the test; re-ran CI."

CI summary: Initial pipeline run had one failing integration test (timing-dependent). After fixing the test harness and adding a small debounce, the pipeline completed: 48/48 unit tests passed, 6/6 integration tests passed. Lint and typechecks green. E2E in sandbox (optional) ran twice to confirm stability (both passed).

Migration notes for SDK consumers (short):
- If you pass a custom token provider: no changes required; the saga composes with your provider.
- If you relied on internal StreamClient internals: a small optional config object is now accepted. See docs/sdks/auth-saga.md for code examples.
- To opt-in to warm-up semantics, set AuthSagaConfig.primeOnOpen = true; default remains false to preserve cold-start characteristics.

Why this is different from previous work: Instead of only unifying retry/backoff tables we centralize lifecycle policy and provide a small, testable orchestration that can be shared across SDK implementations without forcing a single language runtime dependency. This reduces duplicate reauth code paths we have patched during incidents.

Performance/observability notes: Lightweight telemetry was added (no high-cardinality labels). We ran a 30m soak with synthetic traffic at 500rps and observed a 4% reduction in transient 5xxs during token rotation windows compared to the pre-saga baseline.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2026-03-02 after approvals from Ethan, Sofia, and Marco.

If you want to try locally: see sdk/typescript/examples/auth-saga-quickstart and the new docs page.
